questions.q: A cell has a cell membrane, ribosomes and chromosomes, but no cell wall or chloroplast. Which inference best matches the combinations and distinctions used in the Exemplar?
options: A) It must be a typical plant cell because chromosomes occur only in plants.
B) It can fit an animal cell because cell membrane, ribosomes and chromosomes are compatible with animal cells, while cell wall and chloroplast are not required.
C) It must be a bacterial cell because every cell without chloroplast is bacterial.
D) It cannot be a cell because all cells must have a cell wall.
questions.answer: B) It can fit an animal cell because cell membrane, ribosomes and chromosomes are compatible with animal cells, while cell wall and chloroplast are not required.
questions.explanation: The source provides a combination of cell membrane, mitochondria, ribosome and chromosome as appropriate for an animal cell. It also identifies cell wall as a distinguishing feature of plant cells and chloroplasts as plant-specific structures involved in photosynthesis. Therefore the stated combination is compatible with an animal cell rather than requiring a plant or bacterial identity.

questions.q: A microscopic cell has a cell wall but no distinct nucleus. Which reasoning identifies it correctly?
options: A) It is a plant cell because all cells with walls have a well-organised nucleus.
B) It is an animal cell because animal cells lack a distinct nucleus.
C) It is a bacterial cell because the source describes prokaryotes as lacking a distinct nucleus, and bacteria can possess a cell wall.
D) It is a nerve cell because nerve cells have walls and no nucleus.
questions.answer: C) It is a bacterial cell because the source describes prokaryotes as lacking a distinct nucleus, and bacteria can possess a cell wall.
questions.explanation: The Exemplar directly presents the case of a cell with a cell wall but no distinct nucleus and identifies it as bacterial. It also states that prokaryotes do not have a well-organised nucleus. Combining those ideas leads to a bacterial, prokaryotic cell.

questions.q: Which chain correctly links a cell structure to its function and then to an organism-level observation from the source?
options: A) Cell membrane -> controls entry and exit of materials -> helps a cell regulate exchange with its surroundings
B) Chromosome -> performs photosynthesis -> gives leaves their green colour
C) Chloroplast -> carries hereditary characters -> transfers traits from parents
D) Nucleus -> forms the outermost plant-cell layer -> provides rigidity
questions.answer: A) Cell membrane -> controls entry and exit of materials -> helps a cell regulate exchange with its surroundings
questions.explanation: The source calls the cell membrane a selective boundary that controls movement of materials into and out of cells. That function directly explains how a cell regulates exchange with its surroundings. The other options assign functions to the wrong organelles or structures.

questions.q: A learner says, “A unicellular organism cannot respire because respiration needs many tissues.” Which correction is most consistent with the Exemplar?
options: A) The statement is correct because only multicellular organisms respire.
B) The statement is wrong because a single cell in a unicellular organism can perform life functions such as respiration and reproduction.
C) The statement is wrong only for plants, because animal-like unicellular organisms do not respire.
D) The statement is correct unless the organism has chloroplasts.
questions.answer: B) The statement is wrong because a single cell in a unicellular organism can perform life functions such as respiration and reproduction.
questions.explanation: The Exemplar explicitly states that unicellular organisms respire and reproduce. It also says that a single cell can perform all the functions needed in a unicellular organism. Therefore tissues are not a requirement for respiration in such organisms.
